conventions.longitude: -180..+180 degrees left to right, 0 degrees (prime meridian) at the image centre, east to the right
conventions.heightEncoding: 8-bit RGB PNG; v = R*256 + G (0..65535), B = 0; metres = minMeters + v / 65535 * (maxMeters - minMeters)
conventions.heightFiltering: load height PNGs with NO colour-space conversion (linear / NoColorSpace), no premultiply, and decode R,G before any interpolation (or use NEAREST + manual bilinear) - linearly filtering the raw R and G channels separately gives wrong values at 256-step boundaries

height.surface: ice surface (top of Antarctic/Greenland ice sheets)

notes.clouds: greyscale, white = cloud; use as alpha/intensity
notes.night: city lights on a dark blue (not pure black) land/ocean base; subtract/threshold the base if used as an emissive map

height.datum: MOLA areoid (mean radius 3389.5 km; equatorial 3396 km)

ring.layout: radial strip: u = 0 (left) is the inner edge, u = 1 (right) the outer edge; v is constant
ring.radiiNote: radii are an estimate (C ring inner edge to F ring) inferred from the positions of the Cassini division (u~0.70) and Encke gap (u~0.95); the first ~5% of the strip is fully transparent

notes.color: surface albedo at 938 nm seen through the haze (not the orange visible-light appearance)
high-pass-filtered mosaic (relief detail, flat albedo), brightened to Enceladus' high albedo
~39% of the surface (north) was never imaged; that area is a smooth synthetic fill

sky.projection: equirectangular; galactic centre (l = 0, b = 0) at the image centre; north galactic pole at the top; galactic longitude increases to the LEFT (the sky as seen from inside the sphere)
sky.encoding: sRGB, tone-mapped from linear EXR with y = 1 - exp(-2 x)

notes.milkyway: Milky Way glow built from faint Gaia stars; the bright Hipparcos/Tycho stars are omitted, so engine-drawn star points can be layered on top

processing: JPEG: max width 2048, Q82; height: 1024x512, decoded BOX average, original min/max
